core.desktop.welcome.title: Your own assistant, in a few steps
core.desktop.welcome.lead: You answer one question after another. At the end you chat with your assistant in Telegram (it is called a bot there), and your data stays on this computer.
core.desktop.welcome.time: Allow about 30 minutes. You can stop at any time and pick up right here later.
core.desktop.need.title: What you need
core.desktop.need.phone: **Your phone with Telegram.** That is where you will talk to the bot later.
core.desktop.need.card: **A credit card.** Anthropic's AI bills you directly for what you use. The project itself is free.
core.desktop.need.machine: **This computer, and it stays on.** The bot runs here. At the end we ask whether the computer should keep running for it.
core.desktop.need.hint: A Mac mini or another computer that is always plugged in works best.

core.desktop.resume.note: Undoing leaves your data and other programs alone. Docker itself stays installed.

core.desktop.rollback.lead: Other programs and your files are untouched. Docker itself stays on your computer; you can remove it via “Uninstall”.

core.desktop.power.title: Should this computer keep running?
core.desktop.power.lead_mac: The screen turns off after 10 minutes, and the Mac keeps working quietly. That way your bot always answers.
core.desktop.power.lead_win: The screen turns off after 10 minutes, and the PC keeps working. That way your bot always answers.
core.desktop.power.yes_mac: It no longer goes to sleep and starts by itself after a power cut. A Mac mini costs about €10–20 a year in electricity.
core.desktop.power.yes_win: It no longer goes to sleep. A PC uses much more electricity than a Mac mini.

core.desktop.result.filevault: **One thing stays manual:** Your Mac encrypts its disk. That protects your data if someone takes it. After a power cut it therefore waits for your password. Until you have logged in, the bot stays silent, and it cannot tell you beforehand.
core.desktop.result.windows_login: **One thing stays manual:** After a restart, for example from a Windows update, you need to log in once. Until then the bot stays silent.

core.help.commands.title: Commands & backup
core.help.commands.body: This overview any time with /help. Set up the household or see the progress: /onboarding. Change the language of fixed texts: /language. Choose the bot's character (e.g. butler): /persona. See and switch what the bot sends on its own: /reminders. As the owner, see what the AI cost in the last 7 and 30 days: /costs. Backups of your data run encrypted via the server command line (lifeagents backup export|restore) — no longer via the chat.

core.update.fail.interrupted: ❌ The update to {tag} was interrupted midway, for example by a restart. Your system is running, but maybe not completely. The backup from before is at {backup}.
core.update.fail.bot_down: ❌ The update to {tag} stopped during the step “{stage}”, and I, the bot, am not running properly right now. Buttons won't work, please use the terminal. The backup from before is at {backup}.
core.update.todo.heading: What to do next:
core.update.todo.retry: Tap “Try again”. A second run continues where it stopped and usually fixes this.
core.update.todo.later: Try again later, in the terminal with lifeagents update.
core.update.todo.disk: Free up storage space. In the terminal, df -h shows how full the device is.
core.update.todo.security: Don't do anything else and don't install anything by hand. Please report this via “Report a problem”.
core.update.todo.held: Run lifeagents reconfigure in the terminal and enter the information. Then tap “Update now” on the update card again.
core.update.todo.doctor: In the terminal, lifeagents doctor shows what is still wrong.
core.update.todo.terminal_update: Run lifeagents update in the terminal. It continues the update where it stopped.
core.update.todo.rollback: If that doesn't work: lifeagents rollback in the terminal takes you back to {from}. Changes made since the backup are lost.
